steps.content: [Background - Train Corridor]
Everything in the carriage is just right.

The lighting is soft, the carpet plush, and the air carries the scent of leather and hot tea. You step into the corridor, ticket in hand, and make your way forward, following the numbers in search of the room that should be yours.

This was never meant to be a journey worth remembering. After solving several high-profile murders in quick succession, your reputation has grown considerably. Many have requested your services since, and you've grown accustomed to traveling for work by now.
This trip is no different. Just as usual, you're traveling to solve some trouble for a stranger you've never met in some faraway place. They're covering the fare, and you booked your seat in advance.
And so, when the attendant closes her ledger and looks up at you, you never even imagined that there would be a problem.

steps.speaker: Train Attendant
steps.content: I'm terribly sorry, Mr. ${PlayerName}, but I'm afraid there are no vacant compartments left on the train.
steps.female_content: I'm terribly sorry, Ms. ${PlayerName}, but I'm afraid there are no vacant compartments left on the train.

steps.content: ...What?

You try every argument you can think of to persuade her, but no matter what you say, you can't secure a ticket. As the departure time draws closer, you have no choice but to abandon the case and return empty-handed—
I was supposed to investigate a case on the train though? How did I get kicked off before the story even started???
[Exit novel-like presentation. Enter Big CG 1 - Author A]
Oh dear, why are you looking at me? Aren't you going to keep reading?
A woman wearing a monocle is sitting across from you. She tilts her head slightly, resting her chin on her hand as she looks at the pages in your hands, smile on her face.
"The poor detective intended to board the Praeva, only to discover that the train was fully booked..."
What should he do? How will he board this train? And what will happen next?
steps.female_content: What should she do? How will she board this train? And what will happen next?

steps.content: Hehe, I wonder—
You can't help but curl your lip. You close the novel and point your finger at the "author" section.
As if the author doesn't know what happens in her own story.
Isn't that right, Ms. <color=#fb9259>Clementine</color>?
[Background - Clementine's Study]

20 minutes ago

A mansion in Eastside
20 minutes ago, you stepped into this study... or, it might be more accurate to say this dump of books.

Papers and books are scattered throughout the room, with even the towering bookshelves being crammed full. Among the classic literature, several books stand out with particularly eye-catching covers. Even from meters away, you can make out the sensational promotional quotes plastered all over them.

"Highly recommended by the new Speaker of the City Council, Max King! The most moving work of the year!" "Moved all of Eastside in N.F. 116! Even Quinn President can't stop singing praises!" "An unparalleled masterpiece with an ending you'll never see coming! A must-read of this year!"
...These publishers really will write just about anything for sales.
You lower your gaze a little more, and you notice all the books share the same author—<color=#fb9259>Clementine</color>.
Pardon the mess, Chief. I wasn't expecting company.
A pair of hands sets a cup of hot tea down in front of you. You follow the rising steam and find yourself coming face to face with the person who placed it there.
The woman looks at you, beaming. She's wearing a fitted trench coat with a striking butterfly pin fastened at her choker, looking more like a performer than an author.
I've heard some authors use pen names. What about you? Is Clementine your real name?

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: It is, of course.

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: I've heard much about the MBCC Chief, but this is our first time meeting face-to-face. Since you went out of your way to arrange this meeting...

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: Could it be that you're also a fan of my work? Would you like an autograph?
There's laughter in her voice. She's clearly messing with you.

options: I'm afraid I don't read many novels.
Sure, why not? I'm already here.

steps.content: I'm here today to confirm a few things with you.
Sure. But before I get that autograph, I need to confirm a few things with you.
The MBCC received an anonymous tip claiming that you've been concealing your status as a Sinner and using your Mania for personal gain.
Clementine's eyes widen, visibly surprised. Her brow furrows slightly, as if she's genuinely troubled.

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: Hm? Was there an issue with my registration?

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: It's embarrassing, but I must admit—back when I was young and reckless, I traveled everywhere to gather material for my books without ever considering the dangers. Fortunately, apart from the infection, I managed to come away from that time in my life unscathed. But then I got so caught up in writing that even after I learned the regulations had been relaxed, I completely forgot to register myself.

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: I never intended to hide my identity. After all... "Famous Bestselling Author Revealed to Be a Sinner!" sounds like quite the headline, doesn't it?

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: Oh, speaking of which, I have a new book coming out soon. Why don't we work together on this, Chief? We could turn it into a publicity campaign, and who knows, maybe the extra sales might just get us a few bucks—
She seems eager to share more of her marketing wisdom with you, but you cut her off.

A registration lapse wouldn't have been a huge problem. Ever since the parole regulations took effect, B-Class Sinners no longer require supervision under normal circumstances. But the allegations against you go far beyond that—
<color=#fb9259>Every time you publish a new book, a murder case bearing striking similarities to your story occurs in Eastside shortly after. Without exception.</color>

A pianist who murdered their agent the night before a performance. Brothers who turned on each other over an inheritance... And most recently, a serial killer hiding in a rural nursing home—just like in The Patricia Mystery.
Furthermore, you've emphasized the realism in your work on multiple occasions. You claim to have conducted rigorous research, and your stories draw inspiration from real life—
You pick up a book from the woman's desk. On the cover, a massive vintage train is barreling forward. Thick plumes of steam are billowing from its chimney, eventually coalescing into huge letters.
"<color=#fb9259>Murder on the Praeva Express</color>—a crime thriller so vivid, you'll feel like you're physically there at the scene. A murder mystery that will exceed all expectations."
Every one of your novels is followed by a new murder case... Are you predicting these deaths, or are they happening because of you?
Faced with your accusation, Clementine's smile falters ever so slightly.

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: ...Those words are nothing more than a little marketing gimmick. Surely you don't think these works of fiction, meant for entertainment, actually affect reality, Chief?
After receiving the tip, the MBCC attempted to pull your records. But no matter how thoroughly we searched, we found nothing. Every database came up blank for your name.
The name "Clementine" doesn't exist in any official records.
When this novel does get published... who will be the next victim?
You narrow your eyes, studying Clementine's face intently, searching for any crack in her composure. But she simply rests her chin against her hand, tilts her head, and smiles.

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: Now, now, Chief. I'm merely a novelist. I don't have that kind of power. Whenever I do reference real events, I need time to digest the material, to let it simmer before it becomes something on the page—

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: Besides, I've always preferred <color=#fb9259>pure fiction</color> over stories that draw inspiration from reality.
She taps the cover of the book in front of you.

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: Steam trains are energy-inefficient and slow. They're far too outdated for the modern DisCity, and only exist in records from before Nightfall.

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: The current DisCity has no such mode of transport, and stories with that kind of period charm are few and far between. That said, these relics of the past have always had a special place in my heart, and my readers are more than happy to be transported to a world completely unlike their own.

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: A place with no catastrophes, and no Mania—as though you've travelled back into the past. There, you'll find but a leisurely old train, and a story captivating enough to stir the heart.

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: As for why I always emphasize <color=#fb9259>the authentic, lifelike experience</color>...
Clementine's eyes narrow as she raises a finger to her lips, her words laced with hidden implications.

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: Call it a little indulgence of mine. What author wouldn't want to leave their readers in awe?
She opens that novel called "Murder on the Praeva Express" in front of you. Unlike the polished cover, the pages inside aren't fully typeset. You can see handwritten edits amidst the sea of words.

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: That's right. A little, exclusive preview.

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: This kind of VIP treatment is hard to come by, you know. See, my stories are serialized—that means everyone else will have to wait at least two more days before they can read the ending.
Unfortunately, I'm not here as your reader. I'm here for your confession, and I'd love to hear it right now.
Clementine shakes her head with a smile.

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: If you reveal the mystery at the start, no one will buy the book. That's the cardinal rule of marketing.

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: As for whether those rumors are true or false...

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: Why don't you see for yourself? Just what kind of crime story I wrote... and how it came to be.
...It seems she won't talk so easily. You flip through the pages, and a certain keyword catches your attention.

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: That's right. A detective, a victim, and a cold case.

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: The detective gets drawn into the case, and he must investigate the clues before the end comes. He has to cut through the fog to uncover the truth, and identify the <color=#fb9259>real killer</color> among the crowd.
steps.female_content: The detective gets drawn into the case, and she must investigate the clues before the end comes. She has to cut through the fog to uncover the truth, and identify the <color=#fb9259>real killer</color> among the crowd.

steps.content: ...That doesn't sound particularly "safe."

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: But it's a classic setup, and quite engaging, isn't it?
The enigmatic author winks at you.

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: And, perhaps you might even catch a glimpse of the <color=#fb9259>real me</color> through this book!
You frown and turn your attention back to the pages.
In the book, the unfortunate detective has already boarded the Praeva, still fretting over the ticket issue...
[Battle 1, Train Scene]
